SUBJECT: BOR's Draft Environmental Statement for EO11644 concerning the use of ORVs upon public lands
Dear Sir,
I am the "Arctic Representative" for Friends of the Earth, a national conservation organization of over 27,000 members with a membership of nearly 200 Alaskans. Our state has very large areas of Public Domain lands under Federal ownership and management. It is my urgent duty to comment to you upon Interior's EOll644 concerning the use of Off Road Vehicles on public lands and the subsequent Draft Environmental Impact Statement which your department has prepared for the Executive Order.
My comments are made strictly with Alaskan conditions in mind, but with the knowledge that application of these comments is pertinent to other states in which federal ownership is present, including those states in which the Tennessee Valley Authority and the Bureau of Reclamation have lands under their ownership or control. We are of course very especially mindful of interior Alaska's sub-arctic and arctic conditions and also the potential for heavy use of the ORV by all sectors - private commercial, ren-commercial, government, military, recreational and non-recreational - in our state which has few roads and many isolated sites of interest to the ORV user.
FOE appreciates the intent of EOll644, especially since it has, in cooperation with other organizations, instituted its own study of ORV use with an intention of developing model legislation for ORV uses.
FOE in Alaska would like to start with the position that no ORV uses are appropriate on public lands anywhere for any reason in Alaska. We do realize that some uses are necessary however, such as the uses of Natives and some Non-Natives for subsistence activities such as the gathering of firewood, fishing and hunting. In this light we grant that certain uses for ORVs are necessary, but only if under strict control, especially within the fragile ecosystems in Alaska.
We feel that your impact statement draft is vague on important points. Your attempts to relate economic and environmental impacts is incomplete, unrelated to each other, and inappropriate.
